    Small cards. Big trouble.

    Meet the cards that change the game.

    2 · Always Playable

    Universal Play

    Put a 2 on top of anything. It is always legal to play on any card. Any rank may follow unless low turns remain. A 2 consumes one low turn; it does not cancel the remaining seven restriction.

    Table talk A vital lifeline when facing high Kings or Aces.

    3 · Reverse

    Direction & Again

    Reverses play direction. In a 2-player game, you immediately play again! With 3 or 4 players, play passes to the next player in the reversed direction. An even matching set keeps the direction. Note: must still be a legal play matching or beating the pile.

    Table talk In 1-on-1 matches, 3s grant an immediate extra turn to chain your moves.

    7 · Low Cards

    Play ≤ 7 · Stacks

    Forces the next play to be 7 or lower (7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, or low Ace). Stacks: each additional 7 played adds another low turn! Each low play uses one turn. Once all low turns are fulfilled, play resumes from the rank played.

    Table talk Traps opponents who hoarded high face cards.

    10 · Pile Burner

    Burns Pile & Play Again

    Always playable on ANY card. Instantly wipes the entire center pile into the burned graveyard, removes all restrictions, and you play again immediately on a fresh empty pile!

    Table talk The ultimate emergency escape. Stash 10s in your face-up reserve for the endgame.

    A · High or Low

    Rank 14 or 1

    Normally highest rank (14). Beats everything up to Kings. An opening Ace counts as 1. Following a seven-forced low Ace, subsequent Aces offer a choice of 1 or high (14) once all low turns are used. Four Aces burn together regardless of values.

    Table talk High Aces lock down the table; low Aces slip under 7 restrictions.

    Joker · Transparent

    Transparent Mimic

    Always playable on anything. The Joker is completely transparent: the card underneath still sets the rank to beat for the next player. Does not consume a low turn.

    Table talk Safely passes your turn without altering the pile when you lack good plays.

    Four of a Kind · Burn

    Quad Burn & Play Again

    Playing four matching cards burns the pile on ANY card, exactly like a 10! Also, four matching ranks placed consecutively on the pile by any players automatically burns it. Play again.

    Table talk Save sets of 4 in hand to drop them all together for an instant burn.

    1

    The Goal & the Pot

    Start with 1,000 virtual coins. Each seat pays 100, 500 or 1000 coins before the deal; AI contributions are simulated. First out wins the whole pot immediately. Remaining players finish to determine the Shithead. Leaving for the menu pauses your game; replacing it forfeits any unpaid buy-in. With fewer than 100 coins, finish your current wager to unlock a free refill in the main menu. Daily Fortune offers a free 250–2,500 coin allowance once every 24 hours and optional virtual-coin slot spins. Its Payouts & Rules panel explains the odds. Coins have no cash value.

    Be the first to play every card from all your zones. Players who shed all cards escape safely. The last player left holding cards is crowned the Shithead.

    2

    Play Equal or Higher

    Drag a card onto the center pile, or click cards and press Play. Play a card equal to or higher in rank than the top card of the pile, or play a special card (2, 10, Joker, or Four of a Kind).

    3

    Draw Back to 3 Cards

    While the draw deck has cards, draw back up to at least 3 cards in your hand at the end of every turn.

    4

    Matching Sets & Groups

    You can play multiple cards of identical rank together in one turn (pairs, triples, or quads). Tap a card to select its matching rank. Tap selected cards to put them back individually, then drag the selected cards onto the pile. You can also select cards with Space and activate the pile with Enter.

    5

    Can't Play? Pick Up the Pile!

    If you cannot play a legal card (or choose to save your power cards), you must pick up the entire center pile into your hand. Your turn ends immediately.

    1. Blind Face-Down Reserve (3 cards)

    Three cards dealt face-down on the table. No one knows what they are until the very end. Played blind one by one when your hand and face-up cards are gone. Pure suspense!

    2. Visible Face-Up Reserve (3 cards)

    Three cards placed face-up over your blind cards. Before the match starts, swap cards with your hand to stash high power cards (10s, 2s, Aces) here for a smooth endgame escape.

    3. Hand Cards (3 cards)

    Three starting cards held privately in hand. Refilled from the deck as cards are played. You must empty your hand before you are allowed to play your face-up reserve.

    The Swap Phase & Bottle Spin

    After dealing completes, drag or click to swap cards between your hand and face-up reserve. When ready, the brass Fate Needle spins in the center to randomly choose who opens the game with equal odds.

    The Last Stretch (Blind Flips)

    Once the deck, hand, and face-up cards are cleared, pick a face-down card without peeking. If it cannot be legally played, you must pick it up along with the entire pile and play your hand again!

    A fresh deal?

    Your current game will be swept from the table. Any unpaid buy-in is forfeited. A new deal costs its table stake.

    Your wallet and running score stay intact.
